title: Squared level anomaly gave no clear probability forecast gain for Michigan-Huron at 1970-2024 origins
abstract: We tested whether squared distance from the past seasonal mean improves lake level forecast uncertainty. We used coordinated v2025 monthly Michigan-Huron levels for 1918-2025. We made 660 twelve-month forecasts at 1970-2024 monthly origins. The mean forecast was fixed across two Gaussian variance models. Each variance fit used only earlier errors from a past-only forecast archive. Adding squared anomaly changed mean log score by -0.02379 nats per forecast. The conditional 95% five-year block interval was -0.07082 to +0.00423. Mean continuous ranked probability score rose from 13.085 to 13.137 cm. All planned log-gain intervals included zero. The result gives no clear gain for this variance term. It does not prove that uncertainty is independent of lake level. One lake, revised observations, Gaussian tails, simple models and conditional block intervals limit inference. The package contains code, source hashes, aggregate score draws, an independent audit and a figure. Source records and derived record-level forecasts stay external.

display.caption: Log score gain and conditional five-year block intervals. Positive values favor squared anomaly. The right panel sums annual mean score gains; it does not show lake level.
